'''Wesley Deshawn Iwundu''' (born December 20, 1994) is an American basketball player. He played college basketball for [[Kansas State University]].

Iwundu was recruited by coach [[Bruce Weber (basketball)|Bruce Weber]] to [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]] out of [[Westfield High School (Harris County, Texas)|Westfield High School]] in [[Houston]]. He would go on to be a starter from the beginning, breaking the Wildcats' career record for games started with 124.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Robinett|first1=Kellis|title=Wesley Iwundu poised to become K-State’s first NBA Draft pick in nearly a decade|url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/kansas-state/article144031224.html|accessdate=June 4, 2017|work=[[Kansas City Star]]|date=April 11, 2017}}</ref> He came in as a part of a heralded 5-man 2013 recruiting class, but ultimately was the only player who stayed at K-State past two seasons. His perseverance paid off, as he was named third-team All-[[Big 12 Conference]] in both his junior and senior seasons.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Corbitt|first1=Ken|title=K-State’s Wesley Iwundu working for final shot at NCAA Tournament|url=http://cjonline.com/sports/catzone/2017-03-05/k-state-s-wesley-iwundu-working-final-shot-ncaa-tournament|accessdate=June 4, 2017|work=[[The Topeka Capital-Journal]]|date=March 5, 2017}}</ref> For his senior season, Iwundu averaged 13.0 points, 6.3 rebounds and 3.5 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web|last1=|first1=|title=Wesley Iwundu ESPN.com profile|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/67249/wesley-iwundu|accessdate=June 4, 2017|work=[[ESPN.com]]|date=}}</ref>

Following the close of his college career, Iwundu was invited to the 2017 [[NBA Draft Combine]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Robinett|first1=Kellis|title=Former Kansas State star Wesley Iwundu invited to NBA Draft Combine|url=http://www.kansas.com/sports/college/big-12/kansas-state/article147617884.html|accessdate=June 4, 2017|work=[[Wichita Eagle]]|date=April 29, 2017}}</ref>
